findings.issue: Production behaviour of the shared design-system helper was changed to reproduce a known typo in the design reference. Bidi.Wrap now carries a special case (lines 50-63) returning a lone standalone Western digit unisolated, while a lone standalone Latin letter is still isolated. Result: Wrap("القرص D") isolates "D" but Wrap("الجهاز 1") leaves "1" bare, and "الجهاز 1" behaves differently from "الجهاز 12". Nothing in AGREEMENT item 55, DESIGN-GUIDE.md or the rules list at the bottom of docs/design/bidi-test.html distinguishes a digit from a letter — the distinction exists only because the hand-typed «مع العزل» column of that page (case W04) forgot one <bdi>. The prior review (docs/build/reviews/B0-closeout/verify-ui.json, finding 5) prescribed the opposite direction verbatim: fix docs/design/bidi-test.html, "No code change needed". This package's own rule is "otherwise a pure move/rename", and git diff confirms Bidi.cs was otherwise byte-identical to HEAD. Baking the typo into the shared library means every future package (Ar.FirstRun, Admin.UI, the Android kit) inherits a silent, undocumented exception in the one helper all mixed Arabic/Latin text flows through. The builder flagged it for a supervisor ruling; the ruling should be made before Wakeel.Design becomes the shared foundation.
findings.fix: In src/Wakeel.Design/Bidi/Bidi.cs restore the uniform rule: `var wrapped = TokenPattern().Replace(text, m => Lri + m.Value + Pdi);` (delete the `if (m.Value.Length == 1 && m.Value[0] is >= '0' and <= '9') { return m.Value; }` block and its comment). In tests/Wakeel.UI.Tests/BidiWrapTests.cs restore the W04 expectation to `"الحساب " + Isolated("a.khatib") + " · الموظف أحمد الخطيب · الجهاز " + Isolated("1") + " — " + Isolated("PLN-PC-01")` and revert the class doc comment to the earlier 'deliberate, documented deviation' wording. Supervisor (docs/ is outside the builder's allowed paths): wrap the «1» in <bdi> on the W04 «مع العزل» line of docs/design/bidi-test.html so the normative reference agrees, and record the decision in docs/build/BUILD-PLAN.md.

findings.issue: The masked date field loses input the mask rejects and cannot be edited anywhere but at its end. OnDateInputAsync always pushes the reformatted string through ValueChanged; when that string equals the current Value, Blazor's renderer sees no change to the `value` attribute and never rewrites the DOM, so the rejected character stays on screen. Reproduce: type "12", then any letter or space — the field displays "12a" while Value is "12", and it only self-corrects on the next accepted digit. Separately, because the whole value is rewritten on every keystroke the caret jumps to the end, so a user cannot correct the month inside an already-typed "12/09/2026" (typing mid-string appends at the end instead). The happy path is fine — I confirmed live over CDP that typing 12092026 yields 12/09/2026 — this is the edge-case half only.
findings.fix: Give the date <input> an @ref (ElementReference _dateRef) and add a `setInputValue(el, value, caret)` helper to src/Wakeel.Design/wwwroot/js/app.js that assigns el.value then calls el.setSelectionRange(caret, caret). In OnDateInputAsync compute `var formatted = FormatDateMask(digits);` and when `formatted == Value` (nothing for the renderer to diff) call `await Js.InvokeVoidAsync("wakeelUi.setInputValue", _dateRef, formatted, caret)` instead of relying on ValueChanged; otherwise keep the existing ValueChanged.InvokeAsync(formatted). Derive caret from the digit count before the original caret plus the separators inserted ahead of it so mid-string editing keeps its position.

findings.issue: The masked-date behaviour introduced by spec item 7 has zero bUnit coverage. WInputTests covers label/required, value-changed, error, password reveal and textarea, but nothing exercises ResolvedPlaceholder, ExtractWesternDigits or FormatDateMask — the three pieces of new non-trivial logic added to WInput.razor. Nothing in the suite would catch a regression in the Arabic-indic normalisation, the 8-digit truncation, the separator positions, or a revert to <input type="date"> — which is exactly the defect the supervisor's smoke test found. It was verified only manually via CDP this session.
findings.fix: Add to tests/Wakeel.UI.Tests/Components/WInputTests.cs: (a) DateType_RendersMaskedTextInput_WithArabicPlaceholder — render WInput with Type=WInputType.Date and assert input type=="text", inputmode=="numeric", maxlength=="10", placeholder==Ar.Fields.DatePlaceholder, and that the calendar WIcon adornment is present; (b) DateType_InsertsSeparators_AsDigitsAreTyped — capture ValueChanged and assert Input("1")/"12"/"120"/"12092026" produce "1", "12", "12/0", "12/09/2026"; (c) DateType_NormalizesArabicIndicDigits_AndDropsOtherCharacters — Input("١٢٠٩٢٠٢٦") and Input("12a09b2026") both produce "12/09/2026"; (d) DateType_UsesCallerPlaceholder_WhenSupplied.

findings.issue: TextControl_HasPlaintextClass_ForMixedArabicLatinValue is a tautology. Its doc comment claims it covers AGREEMENT item 55 (`unicode-bidi: plaintext` on free-typed mixed Arabic/Latin text), but the single assertion is Assert.Contains("w-field-control", cut.Find("input").ClassList) — a class every WInput emits unconditionally regardless of Type, Value or the CSS. The mixed value "20260912/12046" passed in is never asserted on, so the test still passes if the plaintext rule is deleted from WInput.razor.css or the value is mangled. The file moved verbatim so the weakness is pre-existing, but it is exactly the false-confidence pattern this review is asked to flag.
findings.fix: Make it falsifiable: assert the control passes the mixed string through unchanged and without injected isolates — `var input = cut.Find("input"); Assert.Equal("20260912/12046", input.GetAttribute("value")); Assert.DoesNotContain(Wakeel.Design.Bidi.Bidi.Lri, input.GetAttribute("value")!);` — and cover the CSS contract separately with a test that reads the shipped src/Wakeel.Design/Components/WInput.razor.css and asserts `.w-field-control` still declares `unicode-bidi: plaintext`. Rename the test to match what it actually verifies.

findings.issue:
In UserNameAndRole_RenderAsSingleLineElements the two closing assertions Assert.Empty(name.QuerySelectorAll("br")) / Assert.Empty(role.QuerySelectorAll("br")) are tautological — WTopBar.razor renders @UserName and @UserRole as plain text nodes and has no code path that could emit a
, so they can never fail. The Assert.Single plus exact-TextContent assertions above them are real and do satisfy the spec's requirement to assert the top bar renders the sample user name and role in single-line elements, so this is polish, not a coverage hole.
findings.fix:
Replace the two
assertions with something that can regress: assert the markup contract the CSS depends on — that name and role are siblings inside one .w-topbar-user-text container (Assert.Same(name.ParentElement, role.ParentElement); Assert.Contains("w-topbar-user-text", name.ParentElement!.ClassList);) and that the name element is a (Assert.Equal("BDI", name.TagName)), which is what keeps a Latin-script name from flipping the RTL line.

SECURITY (review item 3) — clean
The only MarkupString in the codebase is WIcon.razor's @((MarkupString)Markup), and Markup comes solely from IconRegistry.g.cs, a compile-time Dictionary of vendored Lucide path data keyed by a developer-supplied icon name; an unknown name yields string.Empty and never caller text. No InnerHtml/innerHTML anywhere. All six JS interop calls are InvokeVoidAsync with fixed identifiers under window.wakeelUi (setTheme, bindCtrlF/unbindCtrlF, trapDialog/releaseDialog); app.js never evals, never concatenates markup, and validates setTheme's argument against 'light'/'dark' before touching the DOM. Nothing secret reaches UI state: FileUiStateStore persists only "theme" and sidebar group open/closed flags under %LocalAppData%\Wakeel, degrading to an empty dictionary on a corrupt or unreadable file instead of throwing. App.xaml.cs's --remote-debugging-port parser still validates the port with ushort.TryParse before forwarding, so extra Chromium switches cannot be smuggled in.

FOR THE SUPERVISOR (not builder defects, no action required from the builder)
1. Ar split: Nav (المراسلات/القضايا/الموظفون/الأصول والعُهد/المالية/التقارير) sits in Ar.Common.cs while Groups (the sidebar section headers) sits in Ar.App.cs. The spec lists "Nav" under Common and "sidebar menu items" under App, which is self-contradictory; the builder split by which W component owns the string. Related: Ar.Common's Footer.VersionLine interpolates AppName, declared in Ar.App.cs, so the "Common" partial is not self-contained today.
